scores.claim_text: 1,744 MW aggregate operating capacity across 10 datacenters as of March 31, 2026; 1,259.5 MW pipeline; 3,003.5 MW total potential.
scores.M_value: 0 third-party mentions of the headline MW figure; capacity narrative appears only in own 20-F.
scores.interpretation: Operating MW figure is large (1,744) but breakdown shows it is overwhelmingly BTC-mining capacity (Rockdale 563, Bhutan 600, Norway 309, Ohio 121, Ethiopia 50). Only Cyberjaya 2 MW is explicitly AI-cloud. Calibration #11: legacy crypto floor space is not equivalent to AI capacity. Total 'pipeline' includes 570 MW Clarington blocked by litigation and 300 MW Niles slated Q4 2028. MODERATE: 1,744 MW operating is real per BTDR's disclosure but conflation of crypto MW with AI/colocation MW in the 'pipeline -> 3,003.5 MW' headline is a planned-vs-operational disclosure-quality issue (Calibration #3).

scores.claim_text: Massillon, Ohio operational 121 MW with 26 MW fire-damaged (Nov 2025) and 74 MW additional phases Q2 2026.
scores.M_value: 404 EDGAR hits but none linked to Bitdeer's Massillon site (top hits: Babcock & Wilcox, PKG, regional banks, REITs); BTDR's Massillon datacenter has no third-party EDGAR mention; bitdeer-specific search returns 0.
scores.interpretation: Site is genuinely operational (impairment recorded; specific MW disclosed; insurance recovery in progress). But: (i) Nov 2025 fire damaged ~26 MW; (ii) usage labeled 'Crypto' not AI per the site chart; (iii) timeline for 74 MW phase-in is Q2 2026. MODERATE underdelivery: a real, in-use site, but with execution slippage and not yet contributing to the AI-pivot thesis.

scores.claim_text: Clarington, OH 570 MW under contract with local utility for colocation; AHP litigation may delay timing.
scores.M_value: AHP search returns exactly 1 hit (BTDR's own 20-F) — confirms the lawsuit exists and is disclosed only in BTDR; 39 hits for 'Clarington Ohio' are all Equitrans / EQT Midstream pipeline filings, none related to BTDR or any utility partner publicly disclosing a 570 MW Bitdeer load.
scores.interpretation: BTDR claims 570 MW power 'under contract' but provides no utility name and no third party (utility, IOU, or counterparty) corroborates a 570 MW load in EDGAR. The site is in active litigation with energization 'to be updated' (i.e., indefinite). The 'colocation' usage label has no named customer. Calibration #3 stage-ladder analysis: this is at most a power MOU stage, not lease/shell/energized. SEVERE: largest single piece of 'pipeline' (45% of 1,259 MW) is at the earliest stage and legally encumbered.

scores.claim_text: Niles, OH 300 MW grid-interconnected site (41.8 acres owned) with utility transmission-line extension agreement, intended for colocation/AI cloud, Q4 2028 energization.
supports: 20-F Item 4 pipeline chart and Datacenters in the pipeline section
scores.M_value: 0 hits — neither BTDR nor any utility partner mentions this 300 MW project in EDGAR (other than BTDR's own 20-F when searching broader terms).
scores.interpretation: Land-owned + transmission-line agreement is an early-but-legitimate development-stage milestone. However Q4 2028 energization is 2.5+ years out; no named customer; usage labeled 'Colocation / AI cloud' (not yet bound). Calibration #3: term-sheet/early-development stage. MODERATE: real grid-interconnect work but very long lead time and zero customer commitments today.

scores.claim_text: BTDR offers AI cloud services in Asia powered by NVIDIA DGX SuperPOD H100/H200/B200 + GB200 NVL72; AI cloud revenue FY2025 = US$6.769M (1.1% of $620M total).
scores.M_check: edgar_fts 'Bitdeer GB200', 'Bitdeer SuperPOD', 'Bitdeer AI cloud'; counterparty CIKs for NVDA/MSFT/AMZN/GOOGL/META/ORCL/AMD/AAPL
scores.M_value: ZERO third-party EDGAR mentions of Bitdeer in any hyperscaler's filings (MSFT 0, AMZN 0, GOOGL 0, META 0, ORCL 0, NVDA 0, AMD 0, AAPL 0). NVIDIA's filings do not mention Bitdeer as a customer or partner despite the alleged DGX SuperPOD + GB200 NVL72 deployments. 'Bitdeer AI cloud' search returns 1 hit (BTDR's own 2025 20-F).
scores.interpretation: AI-pivot narrative is loud (153 mentions of 'AI cloud' / 'AI infrastructure' across the 20-F) but actual revenue is tiny ($6.8M, 1.1%). Calibration #11 (rev-rec pattern) and Calibration #3 (planned vs operational) both apply. NVIDIA does not corroborate the SuperPOD/GB200 deployment in its own filings — these are likely commercial purchases (not strategic-partner status). Two AI-cloud datacenters are tiny: Cyberjaya 2 MW operating + 9.5 MW pipeline (i.e., ~11.5 MW total AI-cloud-labeled capacity vs 1,744 MW total). The headline 'AI infrastructure and AI cloud business' is at term-sheet/early-deployment stage despite 2-year marketing emphasis. SEVERE.

scores.claim_text: Tydal Norway AI conversion EPC contract signed March 27, 2026 with Data Center Installations AS.
supports: 20-F subsequent-events disclosure + filed exhibit (English translation of Tydal Data Center design and execution agreement)
scores.M_check: edgar_fts 'Data Center Installations AS'; edgar_fts 'Tydal Bitdeer'
scores.M_value: DCI EPC contract returns 2 hits — both are BTDR's own 20-F (main document + exhibit). 'Tydal Bitdeer' returns 0 in EDGAR cross-filer search. The exhibit is filed as Ex 4.43 in the 20-F.
scores.interpretation: The contract is verifiable (filed as an exhibit). DCI is a Norwegian specialist; the AI conversion is at the EPC stage, which is genuine progress from term-sheet. PASS at the disclosure level: claim is real, contract is filed, status is honestly described as conversion-in-flight. Note: Tydal Phase 2 (175 MW) is still labeled 'Crypto converting to colocation' in the site chart, meaning revenue from this conversion is not yet in the run rate.

scores.claim_text: Customer concentration: 4 unnamed customers each >10% of FY2025 revenue (B 16.65%, C 15.81%, D 12.20%, E 10.28%), aggregating ~55% of $620M revenue; Customer A (related party) was 19.05% of FY2023; no named external AI hyperscaler customer in any year.
scores.M_check: edgar_fts 'Bitdeer hosting' / 'Bitdeer customer' / counterparty CIK runs
scores.M_value: Zero counterparty disclosure in any hyperscaler filing. Zero external EDGAR hits for 'Bitdeer hosting customer'.
scores.interpretation: Four customers each >10% in FY2025 implies real concentration risk but none are named. Customers B/C/D/E most likely include: SEALMINER bulk-order buyers (FY2025 mining-rig revenue surged to $108M from <$1M), cloud-hash-rate sub buyers, and large hosting clients. None are hyperscalers (corroborated by hyperscaler EDGAR silence). Customer A (BIT Group related-party) hosting role was material in FY2023. Calibration #7: absence of hyperscaler counterparty disclosure is consistent with BTDR's narrative — they do not actually claim hyperscaler revenue — so this is NOT a HARD contradiction. MODERATE: real but non-AI concentration; the marketed AI-pivot is not yet supported by any disclosed marquee customer.

scores.claim_text: Heavy related-party financial dependence on BIT Group (chairman Jihan Wu is co-founder/chairman of BIT Group): $521.8M borrowings; $135.6M crypto receivable; new 6,000 BTC facility Feb-Mar 2026; substantially all crypto held in BIT Group custody.
scores.M_value: 'Jihan Wu' returns 34 EDGAR hits, dominated by BTDR's own 20-F exhibits/certifications and a related Mercurity Fintech filing; no independent counterparty corroboration of BIT Group as a financing source; the structure is disclosed solely by BTDR.
scores.interpretation: Calibration #10 (distress fingerprints): structurally circular financing — BIT Group (controlled by chairman) is simultaneously (a) custodian of substantially all BTDR cryptocurrencies, (b) the largest single lender ($521.8M out of $1.0B total borrowings), (c) the counterparty for BTC-denominated put-option premium ($6.4M Feb 2026), and (d) the counterparty for a 6,000 BTC structured facility entered Feb-Mar 2026. This is a *control-person-financing-control-person* fact pattern. The BIT Assets Collateralized Loan was scaled rapidly from $200M -> $550M (April-Dec 2025) -> $516.4M outstanding by April 2026, on variable rates of 9.0% + reference rate. Operating cash burn $1.74B in FY2025 amplifies the dependence. RED_FLAG_NEGATIVE: this is a textbook governance/related-party-concentration signal even before any AI-pivot question.

scores.claim_text: Cash dropped from $476.3M to $149.4M (Dec 2025); FY2025 operating cash burn $1.74B; financed in 2025 via $751M converts net + $668M RPT loans + $351M equity issuance, plus $375M Feb 2026 5.00% convertible senior notes due 2032.
scores.M_value: 0 third-party hits (only BTDR's own filings). Existence of multiple convert series and the related-party dilution structure is disclosed only by issuer.
scores.interpretation: Calibration #10: heavy/serial convertible issuance ($200M Aug-2024, $200M Nov-2024, $375M Jun-2025, $400M Nov-2025, $375M Feb-2026 = $1.55B aggregate principal of converts in ~18 months) plus $668M RPT loans plus $351M ATM/registered direct equity issuance is classic AI-DC distress-financing footprint. Embedded derivative accounting drove a $444.9M non-cash adjustment that produced BTDR's $65.6M *reported* GAAP profit in FY2025 — without the fair-value swing, the underlying operating loss is large. Diluted loss per share was -$1.43 in FY2025 (vs reported basic EPS of +$0.32). Cash runway absent further dilution looks <12 months given $232M FY2025 capex and rising. SEVERE: financing model is dilutive and concentration-dependent on a related-party lender.
